definition: The seasonal movement of livestock, especially sheep or cattle, between summer and winter pastures.
etymology: From French transhumance, rooted in Latin transhumare, “to move across the ground”: trans- (“across”) joined humus (“earth, soil”). The word preserves the old annual journey from lowland winter grazing to high summer meadows and back again.
usage: By mid-September, the valley roads filled with the bells and dust of transhumance.
